summary.text: The digestive system is the gastrointestinal tract plus helper organs: the tongue, salivary glands, pancreas, liver, and gallbladder.
Its job is to break food into smaller and smaller pieces until the body can absorb and use them.
Digestion runs in three stages: the cephalic phase, the gastric phase, and the intestinal phase.

facts.label: Tract length
facts.value: Roughly nine metres, from mouth to anus

facts.label: Large intestine job
facts.value: Takes water and some minerals back into the blood

items.prompt: You smell bread baking and your gut glands start releasing secretions before you take a bite. Which stage of digestion is this?

options.label: The cephalic phase, the first stage
The gastric phase, in the stomach
The intestinal phase, with enzymes from the pancreas
Peristalsis, which has not yet begun in the esophagus

items.explain: The first stage starts with gland secretions in response to the sight and smell of food, before the food reaches the stomach.

items.prompt: A friend says the stomach does most of the work of digesting dinner. Where does most of the digestion actually take place?

options.label: The stomach
The large intestine
The small intestine
The mouth

items.explain: Most digestion of food takes place in the small intestine; the stomach handles the second stage on the way there.

items.prompt: Water and some minerals are pulled back into the blood late in the process, from what is left of a meal. Which part of the tract does this?

options.label: The large intestine
The esophagus
The rectum
The duodenum

items.explain: The large intestine reabsorbs water and some minerals, while the rectum only passes out the waste.

items.prompt: A student asks why the liver and pancreas are not counted as part of the gut tube itself. What is the best answer?

options.label: They only work while the stomach is empty
They do not take part in digestion at all
They are found only inside the mouth
They sit outside the tract but are associated with digestion

items.explain: Organs outside the GI tract that are associated with digestion are called accessory digestive organs, and they include the liver and pancreas.

items.prompt: Swallowed food keeps moving along the gut wall even when you lie down. What mainly drives it?

options.label: Rhythmic contractions of the wall's muscles
Gravity pulling it downward
Saliva sliding it along
Suction from the anus

items.explain: Peristalsis is a rhythmic muscle contraction that begins in the esophagus and continues along the rest of the tract.

items.prompt: Why does chewing a bite of food for longer help digestion begin?

options.label: It sends the food straight to the large intestine
It breaks food apart and mixes it with saliva's enzymes
It makes the stomach skip its own stage
It removes the need for any later enzymes

items.explain: Chewing breaks food down mechanically and mixes it with saliva, whose enzymes start the chemical breakdown.
